title: Embedded Finance and Banking-as-a-Service
summary: How financial products are embedded into non-financial journeys and delivered through banking-as-a-service partnerships, and where regulatory responsibility sits when the customer relationship is outsourced.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How financial products are embedded into non-financial journeys and delivered through banking-as-a-service partnerships, and where regulatory responsibility sits when the customer relationship is outsourced.
Learning Objectives: Map the roles of licensed providers, platforms and intermediaries in embedded finance
Assess the sponsor firm's oversight of partners and programme managers
Evaluate red flags in fast-growing banking-as-a-service arrangements
Syllabus: Embedded payments, lending, insurance and investment
Banking-as-a-service: sponsor banks, programme managers and middleware
Partner onboarding, AML/CFT controls and reconciliation of client funds
Case studies: partnership failures and supervisory findings
Intended Audience: Supervisors of banks, payment and e-money institutions, lenders and insurers that partner with platforms or distribute through them
Policy, innovation and authorisation staff dealing with new entrants, perimeter questions and open finance
Senior managers coordinating with competition, data protection and consumer authorities
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of banking, payments or conduct supervision is helpful. No technical background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)
